findings.message: Anchor the placeholder alternative at the start of the input. Its missing ^ allows IDs that do not begin with aws:/// to pass validation, after which parsing uses offsets from the original malformed input.
findings.evidence: For xaws:///zone/i-placeholder-a, the second alternative matches aws:///zone/i-placeholder-a. Lines 231–234 then split /zone/i-placeholder-a and return Name="zone" without an error. Previously both alternatives required ^aws. This violates the stated prefix contract.

findings.message: Preserve subsequent slashes when extracting placeholder instance names. Selecting only splitted[1] truncates valid placeholder names.
findings.evidence: For aws:///zone/i-placeholder-a/b, validation succeeds, but lines 231–234 return Name="i-placeholder-a" instead of "i-placeholder-a/b". The previous placeholder capture (%s.*) retained the entire name. Supplied callers pass the resulting reference to GetAsgForInstance and InstanceStatus; their downstream behavior is unavailable.

result.coverage: Inspected TASK.json, CHANGE.diff, the complete staged source, and local parser callers. Compared old and new validation and extraction. Ordinary names with the permitted optional suffix retain their previous extraction behavior, and ProviderID remains unchanged.
limitations: No tests or code execution were performed; examples are source-derived.
Manager and cache implementations and the placeholder prefix definition are not supplied. Downstream lookup or deletion consequences cannot be established.
result.contribution: Established two independent contract regressions with concrete input/output traces; excluded unchanged ordinary suffix handling and ProviderID preservation from findings.
